Meteg after silluq

Alternatively, you can click on an individual Hebrew word to toggle only that word's spacing.

← Back to Meteg after the stress.

The same Unicode code point, U+05BD, represents both silluq and meteg. In a verse-final word, U+05BD on the stressed syllable is silluq; a later U+05BD is meteg only when the stress has been established on an earlier syllable.

Case register

Each case below has at least one source—a manuscript or printed edition—whose last metsil (a neutral name here for a U+05BD that may be meteg or silluq) is later than the last metsil in at least one other source.

In each monospace cell, the first line marks sources that have the later metsil and the second line marks sources that do not. The four positions are M = MAM, A = Aleppo Codex, L = Leningrad Codex, and K = Koren; a dash means no classification is recorded yet for that source.

Additional source observations

Ps. 72:15

  • the Simanim Tanakh: no later mark.

1 Kgs. 7:37

  • the Simanim Tanakh: no later mark.

Job 4:12

  • Cambridge Add. 1753: both strokes.
  • Mikra'ot Gedolot ha-Keter: both strokes.
  • the Simanim Tanakh: both strokes.
  • the Second Rabbinic Bible: first position only.

Image evidence

1 Sam. 17:5

The Leningrad Codex has a meteg after its silluq at 1 Sam. 17:5.

The Aleppo Codex lacks the later meteg at 1 Sam. 17:5.

1 Kgs. 7:37

The Aleppo Codex has a later meteg at 1 Kgs. 7:37.

The Leningrad Codex lacks the later meteg at 1 Kgs. 7:37.
